title: Session-churn prefetch impact on MoE queueing and KV reuse
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note documenting experiments and profiling that investigate how short-lived session churn (many independent sessions with long-context requests but few repeated tokens per session) interacts with our MoE routing, prefetch heuristics, and KV/prefix cache reuse. Goal: find low-risk configuration changes to reduce 95/99 p99 tail latency without increasing token cost significantly.

Context and motivation:
- We observe customer workloads where clients open ephemeral sessions (e.g., chat widgets) that send a long prompt once (20–30k tokens) then stream incremental completions, or conversely many sessions that only use a small portion of a long context then terminate.
- MoE routing and our prefetch strategy currently favor aggressive expert prefetch and per-session KV cache allocation to maximize reuse for steady sessions. But with heavy session churn, this causes: excessive expert hotset churn, small-batch penalty when prefetch populates many experts for only a few tokens, and queueing head-of-line delays for other in-flight requests.

Experiment setup (repro):
- Models: MoE variants derived from Qwen-MoE-32k and a Llama-MoE-like internal test model (approx 12B MoE, 64 experts). Also baseline dense Mistral-32k for comparison.
- Hardware: 4x A100-40GB per serving node, nvlink enabled. Single-request worker pinned to a GPU to simplify traces.
- Workload generator: synthetic session generator simulating N sessions with Poisson arrival (lambda varied), session length distribution Pareto (alpha=1.6) clipped at 32k tokens. Two patterns tested: (A) long single upload then incremental responses; (B) short prompt then early termination.
- Metrics collected: per-token CPU/GPU kernel times, routing time, prefetch time, KV cache hits/misses, queueing latency histogram, expert occupancy by session, effective batch size, token cost estimate. Profiling tools: Nsight Systems traces, rpc traces with per-span timing, and custom eBPF-based latency sampling on host network stack.

Key observations:
1) Prefetch cost dominates on high-churn workloads.
   - When prefetch is enabled with default depth (prefetch top-8 experts and allocate KV buffers per session), average extra latency per request: +6–12 ms for small-batch sessions, but 95p and p99 jump by 2x–3x due to contention on kernel launch queues.
   - The cost is mostly from small matrix-multiplies on cold experts and memory allocations for KV buffers (host->device memcpys). Nsight shows many short-lived kernels (<200us) interleaved causing scheduling overhead.

2) KV cache fragmentation reduces reuse but increases memory pressure.
   - We see many small ephemeral KV buffers per session, most of which are never reused. Memory allocator churn and GPU memory fragmentation lead to occasional CUDA OOM spikes when session churn spikes.

3) Routing decisions amplify impact when affinity changes frequently.
   - Sessions that route to dynamically varying expert subsets cause cross-session expert hotness churn. This triggers load balancing reconfiguration and more prefetch activity, creating reinforcement loops where prefetch increases expert cache misses for other sessions.

4) Dense model baseline has more predictable latency under churn, even if higher steady-state cost. For some workloads the dense Mistral-32k p99 is lower than MoE with default prefetch.

Controlled knobs and test results:
A) Reduce prefetch depth to top-2 experts when session lifetime < T_cutoff (T_cutoff=3 requests). Result: p95 reduced by ~18% and p99 by ~28% for high-churn tests; token-cost increase negligible. Tradeoff: slightly worse quality under some long-lived sessions.

B) Prefetch batching window: coalesce prefetch across sessions arriving within 5ms into a single batched prefetch RPC. Result: reduced kernel launch overhead, fewer tiny kernels; p99 improved by ~22% at moderate arrival rates. Adds complexity to scheduling and increases small receive latency by ~1ms.

C) Adaptive KV allocation: allocate a lightweight ephemeral KV buffer (shallow pointer-backed) for first K tokens (K=64) and promote to full KV storage if the session persists or reuses tokens. Result: reduced memory footprint by ~35% and eliminated most OOM spikes in stress tests.

D) Route-stability penalty: introduce a small routing-stability score that biases gating to previous expert affinity for first R requests (R=2). Slows expert switching and reduces hotset churn. Result: improved cache hit and reduced prefetch churn. But may slightly reduce model diversity for some inputs.

Profiling artifacts (high level):
- Kernel launch histogram: many <200us kernels from small expert matmuls and matmul-adds. These cause scheduling gaps on CUDA stream and increase effective latency for larger kernels following.
- NVLink memcpy stats: prefetch-induced host->device memcpy spikes correlate strongly with client arrival spikes.
- RPC traces: serialization + prefetch RPC + kernel startup often exceeds application-critical SLOs for ephemeral sessions.

Open questions and risks:
- Quality impact quantified only on a small eval set. Need to run quality regression on larger prompt suites to ensure top-2 prefetch doesn't cause unacceptable hallucinations or lower accuracy in safety-critical prompts.
- Interaction with quantized kernels (4-bit) not fully measured; small kernels might be faster on quantized path altering tradeoffs.
- Multi-tenant and Dedicated modes: dedicated customers pin capacity and may prefer steady throughput modifications; need separate config knobs.

Immediate recommendations (short-term changes):
1) Default: enable adaptive prefetch depth (based on session age and observed reuse) behind a runtime flag.
2) Implement ephemeral KV allocation promotion heuristic (safe default: promote after 64 tokens or on second request).
3) Add a per-session routing-stability soft constraint (R=2) to reduce hotset churn.
4) Add telemetry counters for small-kernel rates, ephemeral KV allocation counts, and prefetch batch coalescing hits so we can measure in production.

Planned next experiments:
- Run ablation with quantized kernels for MoE to see if small-kernel penalty is reduced.
- Test implications on Dedicated clusters with pinned expert layout across GPUs.
- Larger quality sweep across 2k prompts for top-2 vs top-8 prefetch.

- collect nsight sys: nsys profile --output session-churn-.. --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range cudaProfilerApi

End of note. This is intentionally a working doc; expect revisions as telemetry and QA results come back.
